text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- In the government's next budget, due to be published on Friday, the culture sector is to receive 4.5 billion crowns making it the only area not to have its budget cut in 1997.
- Sweden is short of water due to dry weather. Its resevoirs should by this time of year be 90 percent full but so far are only at 60 percent.
- Over 3.5 billion Swedish crowns have been spent by Swedish industry on the Internet, and 600,000 Swedes have access to the international computer network, a survey shows.
- Sweden and the European Commission will have to solve their differences over imports of alcohol to Sweden by year-end or a decision will be made in the European courts.
- Pharmacia & Upjohn's heart medicine Fragmin can be used as a substitute for costly surgery. This year sales of the drug are expected to hit one billion crowns.
- Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, currently embroiled in an investigation over some of its funds, is believed to have invested 2.8 billion crowns in Swedish firms, a study shows.
